sections.h2: The quickest way to part with a Duluth house
sections.html:
A Duluth owner can put the house on the market, skip the agent, or accept a cash bid from a buyer who takes the property untouched and closes when you say. Repairs, tenants, liens and your moving date decide which fits.

Duluth, in Gwinnett County, keeps adding people. The mid-2025 estimate is 33,815, up from 31,873 at the 2020 count and 26,600 in 2010. Owners occupy 56.5% of homes, so sellers share the market with a large renter population.

Speed pays off when a roof, kitchen or foundation needs money you would rather not spend, when two mortgages are running at once, or when an estate must be wrapped up.

Five-year figures through 2024 show a middle home value of $400,800 and a middle household income of $95,331. Owners with a mortgage pay about $2,116 a month in ownership costs, and owners without one pay $678. Rent runs near $1,828.

Buyers and tenants come from many backgrounds. About 38.3% of people over 5 speak another language at home, so a flyer or message in more than one language can widen your audience.

Whether you sell by listing or for cash, these figures give you a rough sense of the market before you talk to any buyer.

sections.h2: Two buyer pitches: downtown and the highway corridors
sections.html:
Duluth sits about 25 miles northeast of Atlanta. Its main routes are Interstate 85, Buford Highway, Peachtree Industrial Boulevard, Georgia Highway 120 and Pleasant Hill Road. Residents average 29.9 minutes getting to work.

The old downtown core and the newer commercial corridor along Interstate 85 and Buford Highway attract different buyers: walkable character in one, quick highway access in the other. Highlight the features that match your house:

  • Distance to Interstate 85 and the Pleasant Hill Road corridor for commuters.
  • Closeness to downtown events and the Southeastern Railway Museum for buyers who like a town-center setting.
  • Nearby parks and green space, since the city has been a designated Tree City since 1989.
  • Proximity to shopping and dining along the commercial corridors.

Be accurate about distances and school assignment, and let buyers confirm both for the exact address rather than quoting a boundary from memory.

Duluth bills, collects and disburses its own property tax, separate from the Gwinnett County bill. It uses values from the county's Tax Assessor and a millage rate adopted by the City Council.

For tax year 2026, notices went out at the end of September with a December 15, 2026 due date, and any unpaid earlier-year amounts are added to that bill. The city also adds an annual stormwater fee: for 2026 it is $92.70 for most detached single-family homes and $46.35 for most condominiums and townhomes.

A new owner who has no city bill by October 15 should contact the property tax office. When you sell, have the closing attorney check the city bill and the county bill separately, since each has its own payee.

Gwinnett County's Tax Commissioner takes homestead applications for Duluth owners on a single form that covers every exemption. You need primary residence status on January 1, and an application filed after that applies to the following year.

The office takes applications all year, though the deadline printed on your Notice of Assessment controls whether it counts this year. Plan on 6 to 8 weeks for review. Once approved, an exemption renews itself unless something changes.

A fresh application is needed after turning 62, gaining a disability or veteran status, changing your name, or moving the deed into a trust. Whoever buys your house applies on their own after closing, so your exemption does not travel with the property.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with two tax bills
sections.html:
Because Duluth owners pay both the city and Gwinnett County, a clean sale takes a few extra checks. Work through them in order:

  • Ask the city property tax office for the current balance, including any earlier-year amount added to the bill.
  • Ask the Gwinnett County Tax Commissioner for its balance on the same parcel.
  • Pull your mortgage payoff letter and any lien notices.
  • Tell the closing attorney which exemption, if any, you hold, so the settlement statement reflects it.
  • Agree in the contract how this year's taxes are shared with the buyer.

A cash buyer will run the same checks through a title company. Doing them first means fewer surprises at the closing table, and the payoff amounts come out of the sale price rather than your pocket.

sections.h2: Events and attractions you can mention
sections.html:
Duluth promotes public art, Art Month, Fridays-N-Duluth, Howl on the Green and concerts, along with parks, dining and shopping. The Southeastern Railway Museum preserves and operates historic railway equipment, and the Duluth Fall Festival is held the last weekend in September.

Buyers who like a lively calendar will respond to this, and a house within easy reach of downtown can lean on it. Quote only what you have confirmed yourself.

sections.h2: City offices to contact before selling
sections.html:
The Planning and Development department covers permits, inspections, land use applications and ordinances, and the city code is posted online. If you have a half-finished addition, a deck built without a permit, or a stormwater matter pending, call that department before a buyer's inspector finds it.

The Planning Commission and Zoning Board of Appeals pages show whether a variance or rezoning is being discussed near your lot. The city clerk handles occupational tax and business applications, which matters if you run a business from the house.

Cash buyers still run a title review, so mention open permits, unpaid fees and violations at the start.

Lean toward cash when speed and certainty outrank the last dollar. Lean toward a listing when the house is in good order and you can wait through showings, an inspection and a buyer's loan approval.

Ask every cash buyer for written terms covering price, closing costs, closing date and what follows if the buyer fails to close. Then estimate your take-home after the mortgage payoff, both tax bills and any liens, so you can set it beside a listing outcome.

If the house belongs to an estate or several owners, settle who may sign before anything else, since that question stalls more deals than any other.

Compare the written offers line by line before you answer any of them, and ask for time to review each one.

faqs.q: When does Duluth's own tax bill come due?
faqs.a: The city set December 15, 2026 for tax year 2026, with notices mailed in late September. It publishes the dates each year on its property tax page.

faqs.q: Does a Duluth house carry both a city and a county tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The city bills its own tax and Gwinnett County bills separately, with the city drawing on county assessor values and a rate from its council.

faqs.q: What is the stormwater charge on a Duluth bill?
faqs.a: For 2026 it is $92.70 for most detached single-family homes and $46.35 for most condominiums and townhomes, printed on the tax bill.

faqs.q: How slow is a Gwinnett homestead review?
faqs.a: Plan on 6 to 8 weeks. Filing is open all year, and the deadline on your Notice of Assessment governs the current year.

faqs.q: What is a typical Duluth home value?
faqs.a: $400,800 is the middle value in the five-year figures ending 2024. An individual house can price well above or below it.
